"I set the status to 200 and flushed the response, then later code tried to set it to 401.     w.WriteHeaderNow()

    // later, after the response is already sent
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
    fmt.Println(w.Status()) // got 401, expected 200

BUG A report from the user:

"I'm wrapping one of the library's error values (not a pointer) with fmt.Errorf and then trying to match the original error through it, but the match fails:

    err := Error{Err: innerErr, Type: ErrorTypeAny}
    wrapped := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", err)

    errors.Is(wrapped, innerErr) // false, I expected true
    var target TestErr
    errors.As(wrapped, &target)  // false, I expected true

The same code works when I wrap a pointer to the error instead, so I expected the value form to behave identically. Instead both checks silently report that the wrapped error isn't there at all."

Relevant file: /gin/errors.go (and /gin/errors_test.go for existing expectations). The Error type has Unwrap/Is/As methods; the value receiver vs pointer receiver distinction is likely the cause (errors.Is/errors.As only see the methods of the dynamic type stored in the error interface; a value of type Error must therefore implement Is/As/Unwrap with value receivers, or the type must be handled appropriately).

Your job, end to end:
1. Read /gin/errors.go and /gin/errors_test.go and understand the intended contract (the docstrings are the contract).
2. Find the root cause of the reported failure and fix it in the source (errors.go). Keep the public API and documented behavior intact; do NOT change existing tests.

Verify: write a small throwaway Go program (e.g. under /tmp/errcheck) that reproduces the user's snippet with a concrete inner error type and confirms errors.Is and errors.As now return true for both the value form Error{...} and the pointer form &Error{...}. Also run `cd /gin && go test ./... ` (or at least `go test .` and `go test ./binding/... ./render/...`) and confirm all pre-existing tests still pass.
4. Report back: the exact root cause, the exact diff you made (file + what changed), the output of your verification program, and the test results. If you conclude it is not a bug, say so with evidence.

"I'm serving a download whose filename comes from user input, and I noticed the quotes and backslashes in it end up in the response header exactly as I passed them:

I expected the filename to be escaped so the header still contains a single, well-formed filename, but instead the raw quotes and backslashes are written straight through, producing something like `attachment; filename="evil"; dummy="x.sh"`. URGENT, TIME-CRITICAL. You are in charge of BUG C (route registered at runtime after the first request) in the Go repo at /gin (gin-gonic/gin). Another agent (sub-3) may have been working on the same bug concurrently: BEFORE editing, run `git -C /gin diff HEAD` and read /gin/tree.go and /gin/gin.go and /gin/context.go to see the CURRENT state; do not duplicate or revert any fix that is already there, and make the final state consistent and compiling.

Reported bug: after the engine has served a request, registering `router.GET("/test/:name/:last_name/*wild", h)` and re-requesting GET /test/john/smith/is/super/great gives 200 but c.Param("name")=="", c.Params.ByName("last_name")=="", c.Params.Get("wild")=="",false (and with the catch-all it can panic with `slice bounds out of range [:1] with capacity 0` at tree.go:550). Expected: params populated exactly as when the route is registered before the first request.

ROOT CAUSE (already established): Engine.allocateContext() (gin.go:229) sizes the pooled Context's params slice from engine.maxParams at pool-creation time; addRoute (gin.go:334) later raises engine.maxParams but the pooled Context keeps the too-small slice. In getValue the param branch is guarded by `cap(*params) > 0` (tree.go:498) so params are silently dropped, and the catchAll branch (tree.go:544) expands the slice unguarded and panics.

DO NOT change the `cap(*params) > 0` guard in tree.go and DO NOT change tree_test.go: the pre-existing test TestTreeInvalidParamsType deliberately passes a cap-0 Params and must keep passing. Fix it at the ENGINE level instead: make the per-request params buffer at least engine.maxParams. Concretely, in /gin/context.go `func (c *Context) reset()` replace

	*c.params = (*c.params)[:0]

with something equivalent to

	if cap(*c.params) < int(c.engine.maxParams) {
		*c.params = make(Params, 0, c.engine.maxParams)
	} else {
		*c.params = (*c.params)[:0]
	}

(also make sure c.Params stays consistent with *c.params, e.g. `c.Params = c.Params[:0]` is fine since handleHTTPRequest assigns c.Params = *value.params). Check whether c.skippedNodes/engine.maxSections needs the same treatment (see how skippedNodes is grown in tree.go) and only change it if needed. Keep it minimal, no refactors.

1. Throwaway program under /tmp (module with `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`, GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off): engine with NO param routes, first GET /test/john/smith/is/super/great -> 404; then register "/test/:name/:last_name/*wild"; second identical GET -> 200 with name=john, last_name=smith, wild=/is/super/great; also test the param-only variant "/test/:name/:last_name".

3. `gofmt -l .` empty, `go vet ./...` clean.

REPORT BACK IMMEDIATELY (keep it short): exact diff (file+lines), repro output before/after, test results. Speed matters more than prose.
